text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 0.71% today and is down 10% over two weeks, with most of the damage occurring after the company announced quarterly earnings and a leadership change on November 3rd. The broader headwind is visible in refining economics: while U.S. crude trades at $103/barrel, the global benchmark sits at $123/barrel—a $20 gap that squeezes refinery profit margins when they have to buy expensive global oil but sell into a softer U.S. market. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity, elevated but not straining, which means there's limited upside from operating harder.

The company's recent earnings announcement appears to have disappointed investors, possibly because guidance signaled caution rather than strength ahead. Industry commentary from late October warned that Big Oil earnings, while growing, might not translate into stock gains—and that's exactly what's playing out here as MPC trades lower despite solid utilization rates.
